sara (cust-success): Heads-up: ACME reports their quantized endpoint (int8 calibrated) is both slower and slightly lower quality than FP16 after yesterday's deploy. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~380ms. They opened a support ticket and want a short-term mitigation.
josh (eng-runtime): Ugh. Do we have the endpoint name, model, deploy id and a repro prompt? Also any perf traces they can share?
sara (cust-success): Endpoint: acme-chat-prod-1, model: openllm-7b-v2, deploy: dpl-2026-03-17-9pm. Repro prompt: "Summarize the meeting notes" (short). Customer attached a flame graph + p95 histogram. I'll drop snippets.
priya (eng-ml): Can you paste the kernel selection profiler and kvcache logs? suspect fallback to slower kernels or cache thrashing.
sara (cust-success): Paste from their profiler (sanitized):

```
[2026-03-17T21:05:12Z] request id=xyz kernel=quant_int8_perchannel selected
[2026-03-17T21:05:12Z] perf: forward_time=3.8ms per_block
[2026-03-17T21:05:12Z] kvcache: hit_rate=0.12 evict_count=420
[2026-03-17T21:05:12Z] batching: batch_size=1 avg_batch_wait=1.2ms
[2026-03-17T21:05:12Z] kernel_fallback: layer=15 reason=scale_outlier
[2026-03-17T21:05:12Z] request id=xyz kernel=slow_scalar_gemm used
```

They also included a small transcript where latency spikes on first token and remains elevated.
marco (eng-platform): Also sharing the endpoint config: max_batch=8, max_latency_ms=50, autoscale=min=1 max=6. Given low qps the runtime often sends single-request batches. That can kill INT8 perf benefits.
josh (eng-runtime): Right — int8 kernels rely on throughput/pipelining. If batch_size==1 & a layer hits scale_outlier and we fall back to scalar_gemm, p95 explodes. The kvcache hit_rate=0.12 suggests prefix reuse is low too -> repeated KV warmups.
priya (eng-ml): The "scale_outlier" fallback is telling: their calibration likely produced per-channel scales with heavy tails. Per-channel quant can produce occasional extreme multipliers; we detect that and fallback to safe path. We need to see the calibration stats. Ask customer for quant-stats.json (scale histograms).
sara (cust-success): Customer sent a small calib report, excerpt:

```
layer_15: scale_mean=0.023 scale_std=0.042 scale_max=3.4 scale_99=0.78
layer_16: scale_mean=0.018 scale_std=0.004 scale_max=0.11
global: per_channel=true method=histogram_bins=256
```

They mention they calibrated on a short tail of prompts (500 examples) — might be too small and noisy.
priya (eng-ml): That layer_15 scale_max=3.4 is a huge outlier, explains fallback. Two paths: 1) re-run calibration with better representative dataset (drop noisy examples, apply clip/percentile cap), or 2) force that endpoint to prefer FP16 kernels (disable int8 at runtime) as a short-term mitigation.
josh (eng-runtime): Short term I can push a knob to prefer_fp16 for that route so kernel selector avoids int8. That should get p95 back near FP16 numbers quickly. Longer term we should re-calibrate and maybe enable per-layer clamp/percentile (e.g., 99.9 -> 99.0) to reduce outlier sensitivity.
alex (oncall): I can run a canary patch to force prefer_fp16 on acme-chat-prod-1 and measure. Will run in the canary pool for 10m and report p95.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started: canary-id=can-2026-03-18-09:42:15 user=alex route=acme-chat-prod-1 config_override={"prefer_fp16":true}
emily (customer): Quick update from my side: we accepted the temporary FP16 override. Latency dropped to ~140ms p95 on the canary and customers see responses resume. Quality-wise: a tiny change in tokenization output (minor rephrasing), but overall acceptable for now. Thanks.
priya (eng-ml): Good. For a proper fix we should re-run calibration with a larger dataset (2-5k examples) sampled from production prompts and run the new quant-stats through our outlier clamp pipeline. Example command we use:

```
redwood-quant calibrate --model openllm-7b-v2 \
  --data /mnt/calib/acme-2k.jsonl \
  --method per_channel --clip-percentile 99.0 \
  --output /tmp/acme-7b-v2-quant-stats.json
```

Then we validate on the eval prompt-set and perf harness.
josh (eng-runtime): I'll create a short-lived flag to record when fallback to scalar_gemm happens and emit metric per endpoint so we can alert earlier.
marco (eng-platform): Also increasing batch window to 5ms (from 1ms) for low qps endpoints could help increase average batch size without hurting SLOs too much. We'll experiment in staging.
sara (cust-success): I'll coordinate collection of representative prompts from ACME and schedule a calibration rerun with Priya. Also send a friendly note to ACME about the temporary FP16 override and ETA for full fix.
emily (customer): Appreciated. Please include rough timelines in the note — product team wants a fix in the next 48 hours if possible.
alex (oncall): Canary finished: canary-id=can-2026-03-18-09:42:15 results: p95=138ms (down from 380ms), error_rate unchanged. Rolling the override to 10% for now. :thumbsup:
josh (eng-runtime): Filed GH issue: redwood/runtime#4621 "kernel-fallback-outlier-detection-and-mitigation" with steps and links to logs/dashboard: https://perf.redwood.internal/dash/ACME-quant
sara (cust-success): Thanks team. I'll send the customer update and close the support ticket once we complete calibration rerun and validate. :eyes:
priya (eng-ml): TL;DR: cause=calibration outlier on layer_15 -> kernel fallback to scalar gemm + low batching + low kvcache reuse => p95 spike. Short-term=prefer_fp16 override. Medium-term=re-calibrate with larger sample + clamp and tune batch window/kv heuristics.
marco (eng-platform): I'll spin up an experiment to tweak batch window and autoscale to see if we can avoid single-request batches for low qps routes.
emily (customer): Thank you all. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
